phrases.latin: Quid, lubet? pergin' ructāre in ōs mihi? — Suāvis ructus mihi est. Sīc sine, Simō.
phrases.english: What, you feel like it? Will you keep burping in my face? — My burp is a sweet one. Leave me be, Simo.

phrases.latin: in Pompōniō cōnsulārī poētā nōn ructāsse
phrases.english: of Pomponius, the consular poet, that he never burped

sources: Lewis & Short: ructo · Lewis & Short: ructus

Plautus checked against the Perseus Latin texts text of the Pseudolus, printed here with the house apostrophe in pergin'; Pliny in Mayhoff’s section numbers. Not in Traupman or Morgan–Owens in the sections swept; added from Lewis & Short.
